masteryZone.q: Which charter granted the Dutch East India Company (VOC) the authority to wage war, build fortresses, and conclude peace treaties?
opts: A charter granted by Queen Elizabeth I in 1600
A charter granted by the States-General of the Netherlands in 1602
The Treaty of Tordesillas of 1494
A decree of Emperor Jahangir in 1616
masteryZone.sol: The VOC was formed in 1602 under a charter from the States-General of the Netherlands, which gave it corporate state-like powers to declare war, build forts, and make treaties.

masteryZone.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the early Dutch settlements:
1. The first Dutch factory was established at Masulipatnam in 1605.
2. The Golconda Sultan granted the Dutch concessions to establish their first base.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
opts: 1 only
2 only
Both 1 and 2
Neither 1 nor 2
masteryZone.sol: Both statements are correct. In 1605, the Dutch established their first factory at Masulipatnam, Andhra Pradesh, after securing trading rights from the Sultan of Golconda.

masteryZone.q:
Assertion (A): Chinsura became the most important Dutch base in Bengal.
Reason (R): The Dutch established their factory at Chinsura in 1653 and built Fort Gustavus to export silk, saltpetre, and opium.
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
masteryZone.sol: Both Assertion and Reason are true, and R is the correct explanation. Chinsura was the main base in Bengal, protected by Fort Gustavus, and acted as their chief exporting center.

masteryZone.q: Which of the following Dutch factories were established on the Coromandel Coast? (Select all that apply)
opts: Masulipatnam
Pulicat
Nagapatam
Cochin
masteryZone.sol: Masulipatnam, Pulicat, and Nagapatam are located on the Coromandel (eastern) Coast. Cochin is located on the Malabar (western) Coast.

masteryZone.q: Match the local experts who helped in the compilation of 'Hortus Malabaricus' with their association:

options.text: C. Dutch Governor who patronized the work

masteryZone.sol: Itty Achuden was the Ezhava physician; Ranga Bhat/Appu Bhat were Brahmin scholars; Hendrik van Reede was the patron Governor.

masteryZone.q: The Dutch revolutionized the Indian trade by focusing primarily on exporting Indian cotton textiles to the East Indies to purchase spices.
masteryZone.sol: True. The Dutch commercial strategy revolved around exchanging Indian cotton textiles for spices in Southeast Asia, turning cotton into a major export item.

masteryZone.q: The Battle of Bedara (1759) resulted in which of the following outcomes?
opts: The expulsion of the Portuguese from Goa
The decisive defeat of the Dutch, ending their political power in India
The defeat of the French under Count de Lally
The annexation of Awadh by the British
masteryZone.sol: The Battle of Bedara (1759) was a decisive defeat for the Dutch forces at the hands of the British, ending Dutch political aspirations in India.

masteryZone.q: The Dutch formally ceded all their Indian settlements to Great Britain under the Anglo-Dutch Treaty of ________.
masteryZone.sol: The Anglo-Dutch Treaty of 1824 formally cede all remaining Dutch territories in India to Britain in exchange for Dutch supremacy in Sumatra.
